correctness.rationale: For ka=3 the full 2x2 Cournot Jacobian, differentiated before diagonal restriction, has eigendirections (1,1),(1,-1) with transverse eigenvalue 4(1-2eta u), eta=(2+c)/(2+c+d), where diagonal u follows u->4u(1-u). The arcsine invariant law is ergodic via circle-doubling conjugacy; the logarithm is integrable despite at most one zero. Jensen cosine integral yields lambda=log(2eta) for eta>=1/2 and lambda=log(2(1-eta+sqrt(1-2eta))) otherwise, including the singular neutral boundary eta=1/2. For d∈[0,1], s=2+c>2 implies eta>s/(s+1)>2/3, yielding strict lambda>log(4/3), approached at c->0,d=1. For d=s exactly the two coordinates acquire the same multiplicative factor, conserving x/y; expansion d->s± gives linear/square-root one-sided cusps. Almost-everywhere statement is with respect to the natural invariant diagonal logistic measure, not all trajectories.
